name: Robert Saleh

views.text: Fast and violent is the identity, and fans at home should be able to feel it.
Calling the defense keeps a head coach connected to his players instead of just managing the clock.
There is no handbook for a first head-coaching job; the lessons from a failed one are the handbook for the next.
A young quarterback needs time, and the league's impatience does not get to decide when he is finished.
Third down, two-minute and the red zone are where a quarterback proves himself.
Throwing across your body is not a style; it is a turnover waiting to happen.
Coaches should invest in players the way they would in their own kids.
A rebuild built to win championships takes patience, and shortcuts only set it back.
Fighting a teammate ends your day; the standard is about football, not pride.

signatures: answers a question about identity with a short, repeatable slogan
defends a young player against outside criticism before talking about the player's mistakes
stops practice to cool things down after a fight rather than letting it ride
want: to prove in Tennessee that the lessons from his Jets firing make him a winning head coach the second time
fear: that a second head-coaching failure confirms the doubts from New York
voice: High-energy, warm and conversational, with quick, catchy phrases players and fans repeat. He is candid about what he learned from failing in New York, defends his players hard in public, and turns blunt and clipped when a quarterback's mistake or a fight crosses his standard.

evidence.summary: Feature at his hiring (updated 2023): left banking for coaching after his brother survived 9/11, family and faith are central, a father of seven, the first Muslim head coach in the league; described as energetic, people-oriented and competitive, and Shanahan praises the environment he built in San Francisco.

At his introduction he explains his motto as about the daily process of preparing, recovering and communicating, calls coaches and players partners, says coaches should invest in players like their own children, and frames the rebuild as patient work aimed at championships.

After rookie camp, players describe his enthusiasm as constant in meetings and on the field and say they already relate to him. The writer notes personality alone will not win games. Early impressions only.

evidence.publisher: ESPN (Rich Cimini), via ABC7 New York
evidence.summary: He defends Zach Wilson as a young quarterback with a bright future, criticizes the league's impatient culture with a coffee metaphor, praises his late recovery in a game, and says draft status plays no role in who starts. His own words.

On a radio show he declines to explain why Wilson has not been benched, calls the questions fair and says he must weigh the whole team and the film; the writer describes him as flustered. One interview, editorialized.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press (Dennis Waszak Jr.), via ClickOrlando
evidence.summary: AP profile of his defensive coordinator: Ulbrich credits Saleh with his opportunity and support, Saleh praised him often and predicted he would be a head coach, and the Jets blocked a 2023 interview request to keep him. Written the day after Saleh's dismissal; used here only for the working relationship.

Introduction: he will call the defense himself; wants a fast, violent, confident team that plays with swagger and trash talk fans can feel; says there is no handbook for a first-time head coach and that his 20-36 Jets years made him better prepared; praises Daboll as his OC and the organization's people; Ward and Simmons attended. Team-written.

Cam Ward on the new staff: calls Saleh a great hire for the team's identity, respected across the league, and says he is excited to win for him though they have only just met; describes Daboll as fiery and wants that tough coaching. The player's view, early.

Bradley's introduction: hired by his longtime friend Saleh after working together in Seattle, Jacksonville and San Francisco; Saleh calls the defense on game days while Bradley runs it during the week; they share a clear sense of the standard. Team-written.

Camp log through Aug. 11: says the defense will strain any quarterback and joint practices will give Ward new looks; names third down, two-minute and red zone as a quarterback's tests; calls throws across the body non-negotiable and one Ward pick a poor decision; stopped practice for a cool-down talk after Simmons swung at a teammate and sent him off; spoke warmly of Shanahan after his car accident.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (NYJ HC to 2024, SF DC 2025, now TEN HC calling the defense). Added 2026 sources E7-E10 (introduction, Ward on the staff, Bradley hire, camp). Views, want, fear and voice rewritten for Tennessee; sliders unchanged (the 36 budget is used; E7 and E10 show a sharper edge, reflected in the voice). New ties: Bradley, Daboll, Cam Ward.
